about.purpose: The purpose of the Heart of Oklahoma Corvette Club (HOCC) is to encourage participation of the club members in events and social activities that promote HOCC and its membership. The members of HOCC are willing to support those in need, assist with charitable events and support our local schools and other community activities.

officers.name: Dianne Dunbar
officers.bio: Dianne is retired. She is a Veteran of the US Air Force. She has worn many different hats during her career; she is most proud of her work as a private caregiver for the last 15 years. She is thrilled to have found her Corvette family with the Heart of Oklahoma Corvette Club and learning more about her car.

officers.name: David Finley
officers.bio: David currently works for the USDA - NRCS. David’s service is as a Quality Assurance Inspector for the rehabilitation of flood control dams. David’s hobbies include woodworking and diy projects. David enjoys being a part of the Corvette community and hanging out with his Corvette family of friends.

officers.name: Myra Finley
officers.bio: Myra has been married to David for 30+ years and is retired. Myra has over 40 years in the accounting industry. Myra enjoys crafts and diy projects. Myra loves her Corvette and Corvette family.

officers.name: Carolyn Thompson
officers.bio: Carolyn retired from a non-profit after 17 years as a contractor at Tinker Air Force Base. Loves all corvettes but has a special place in her heart for C3’s. Enjoys flowers, woodworking and grandkids.

items.name: Autism Oklahoma
items.text: AutismOklahoma had grassroots beginnings in 2002 when families began meeting together to help problem solve family challenges. We create opportunities and engage families to help their own family and a few more. Our programs are FREE or NEARLY FREE and are funded by donations. 95 cents of every dollar donated is used to fund programs in Oklahoma. 501(c)3

items.name: Sgt. Miles Tarron Foundation
items.text: The Sergeant Miles Tarron Foundation serves so many in their community of McAlester, OK. It all began when Reed Marcum realized some of his classmates didn’t have some of the basic things they needed for school. He started by filling bags with pencils, erasers and other school supplies. This project grew into filling backpacks with school supplies and giving them away to kids in the community. The next phase began with giving away hats and gloves to those that didn’t have any for the winter. This project grew into the largest community toy giveaway in the McAlester area. To date, they have given away over 70,000 toys and there is no sign of slowing down. The Foundation also has a side that honors Veterans with a Field of Honor that consist of flags (made in the USA) and tags for all the Veterans being honored. There is also a scholarship program for high school seniors that includes writing an essay about “What Veterans Mean to Me”. This amazing Foundation has such a tremendous impact in and around the McAlester community doing so many different things for those in need. These different projects began as simple 4-H ideas that were fueled by the passion of those that saw a need and followed their hearts.
